paragraphs: Zymeworks is a global biotechnology company managing a portfolio of licensed healthcare assets and developing a diverse pipeline of novel, multifunctional biotherapeutics to improve the standard of care for difficult-to-treat conditions, including cancer, inflammation, and autoimmune disease. We believe our asset and royalty aggregation strategy differentiates us from other biotechnology companies because it provides us with an opportunity to optimize future milestone and royalty cash flows and selectively invest in high-quality assets while retaining the flexibility to return capital to stockholders.

Our strategy is focused on compounding long-term stockholder value through a combination of royalty growth, strategic acquisitions, and internal innovation, supported by disciplined capital allocation and a strengthened financial foundation through expected milestone payments and royalties from existing commercial partners. We pursue this strategy by discovering or acquiring and developing a diversified portfolio of preclinical or clinical healthcare assets while also evaluating strategic partnership opportunities to transfer certain costs and risks related to clinical development and/or commercialization to our strategic partners and secure the right to receive potential future royalty and milestone revenues. The following elements collectively support the execution of our strategy.

We seek to leverage our expertise in protein engineering and drug chemistry to discover and develop next-generation antibody-based therapeutics to address significant unmet medical needs, particularly in hard-to-treat diseases. Our proprietary structure-guided molecular modeling, combined with internal antibody discovery and generation technologies, supports a fully integrated drug development engine capable of efficiently advancing a pipeline of innovative product candidates.

Our pipeline of multifunctional therapeutics is supported by our multispecific antibody therapeutics ("MSATs") and antibody-drug conjugates ("ADCs") technology platforms, which enable the development of novel therapeutics in cancer, inflammation, and autoimmune disease and create opportunities for new partnerships.

Partnerships and collaborations are central to our strategy as a potential source of funding for ongoing research and development while also reducing reliance on internal capital for later-stage clinical development of partnered assets. These arrangements enable risk sharing, particularly in late-stage development, and support disciplined R&D investment, which can reduce the need to use future milestone and royalty payments to fund planned operations.

Through our asset and royalty aggregation strategy, we seek to optimize future cash flows from a growing portfolio of licensed products and product candidates, including Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) and pasritamig. As partnered therapies advance through late-stage development and commercialization, we expect to grow durable and predictable cash flows that can be deployed by us in order to seek attractive risk-adjusted returns for stockholders.

Our capital allocation strategy is focused on balancing investment in long-term growth with returning capital to stockholders. As our royalty portfolio matures and generates excess capital beyond the needs of our operations and strategic investments, we maintain the flexibility to opportunistically allocate capital to stock repurchases. We view stock repurchases as a potential tool to strategically reduce our share count and enhance total stockholder return over time, while continuing to prioritize investments that can help support sustainable value creation. Decisions regarding capital returns are evaluated within the context of our liquidity position, future cash flow outlook, and overall strategic objectives.

We intend to evaluate and selectively acquire programs, technologies, product candidates and/or companies with high-quality assets or partnerships that align with our strategic objectives. By applying our scientific expertise, development capabilities, and
operational efficiencies, we seek to enhance asset value and generate new royalty streams. In evaluating acquisition opportunities, we consider multiple factors, including:
•Strategic fit; •Royalty potential; •Differentiated assets or platform; •Potential to address an unmet medical need;
•Adequate intellectual property protection; and

We maintain a portfolio of partnered programs that leverage our technology platforms and scientific expertise while enabling risk-sharing and the potential for near-term milestone and royalty-based returns.

Zanidatamab, our first internally developed product candidate to receive regulatory approval, illustrates the execution of this partnership-based approach. Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii), a bispecific antibody targeting HER2-expressing tumors developed using our Azymetric platform, has demonstrated positive late-stage clinical results and achieved regulatory approvals for the treatment of HER2-positive ("HER2+") (IHC 3+) biliary tract cancer ("BTC") in multiple jurisdictions including the United States, China, Europe and Canada. We have entered into separate collaboration and license agreements with BeOne Medicines Ltd. (formerly BeiGene, Ltd. and, together with its affiliates, "BeOne") and Jazz Pharmaceuticals Ireland Limited, a subsidiary of Jazz Pharmaceuticals plc (collectively with their affiliates, "Jazz"), granting each partner exclusive rights to develop and commercialize zanidatamab in different territories. Jazz intends to complete the supplementary biologic license application ("sBLA") submission for zanidatamab in the first quarter of 2026 for the treatment of first-line HER2+ locally advanced or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma ("GEA") under the real-time oncology review program in the United States, where zanidatamab has been granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation for patients with HER2+ GEA. Additionally, zanidatamab is currently being evaluated in multiple global clinical trials for treatment of broader HER2-expressing indications including neoadjuvant populations, breast cancer, and other HER2-expressing cancers. Our partnerships with Jazz and BeOne reflect our strategy of advancing internally discovered programs through collaborations that share development risk while preserving the potential for long-term royalty and milestone revenues.

In addition to $53.0 million already received for regulatory approval of Ziihera in BTC, we are entitled to receive up to $440.0 million in near-term milestone payments from Jazz and BeOne related to approvals of Ziihera in GEA in the United States, Europe, Japan and China as follows: U.S. - $250.0 million; EU - $100.0 million; Japan - $75.0 million; China - $15.0 million. We also expect that royalty revenue from Ziihera sales will increase as potential regulatory approvals are obtained in global markets for GEA.

headings: Our adoption of a royalty-driven asset aggregation strategy is unproven and may not be successful.
Strategic transactions could disrupt our business, cause dilution to our stockholders and otherwise harm our business.
Our long-term prospects depend upon successfully discovering or acquiring favorable assets and progressing the assets through preclinical and clinical development.

Successful development of our current and future product candidates is uncertain, and we may discontinue or reprioritize the development of any of our product candidates at any time, at our discretion.
We may not be successful in our efforts to use our therapeutic platforms to build a pipeline of product candidates.
Our business may become subject to economic, political, regulatory and other risks associated with international operations.
Our business has been in the past and may in the future be adversely affected by public health outbreaks and pandemics.
We face significant competition in seeking new strategic partners.
Risks Relating to Development of Product Candidates

The outcome of clinical trials is inherently uncertain, and current and planned clinical trials may not satisfy the requirements of the FDA or comparable regulatory authorities outside the United States.
If we, or any of our strategic partners, are unable to enroll patients in clinical trials, we will be unable to complete these trials on a timely basis or at all.
The design or execution of clinical trials may not support regulatory approval.
Interim, preliminary or top-line data may change as more patient data become available and are subject to audit and verification procedures that could result in material changes in the final data.
The Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations received for zanidatamab may not result in faster development, regulatory review or approval process.

Additional discussion of the risks summarized in this risk factor summary, and other risks that we face, can be found below under the heading "Risk Factors" and should be carefully considered, together with other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and our other filings with the SEC, before making an investment decision regarding shares of our common stock.
•Our adoption of a royalty-driven asset aggregation strategy is unproven and may not be successful.

•Our long-term prospects depend upon successfully discovering or acquiring favorable assets and progressing the assets through preclinical and clinical development.

This Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the following sections, contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 and the Exchange Act. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results and events to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such forward-looking statements. For a detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties, see Item 1A, "Risk Factors" of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. We caution the reader not to place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements, which reflect management's analysis only as of the date of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. We undertake no obligation to update forward-looking statements to reflect events or circumstances occurring after the date of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for fiscal 2024 as compared to fiscal 2023 has been omitted from this Annual Report on Form 10-K and is incorporated by reference from our Annual Report on 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the SEC and with the securities commissions in all provinces and territories of Canada on March 5, 2025, under the section titled "Part II, Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations."

Zymeworks is a global biotechnology company managing a portfolio of licensed healthcare assets and developing a diverse pipeline of novel, multifunctional biotherapeutics to improve the standard of care for difficult-to-treat conditions, including cancer, inflammation, and autoimmune disease. We believe our asset and royalty aggregation strategy differentiates us from other biotechnology companies because it provides us with an opportunity to optimize future milestone and royalty cash flows and selectively invest in high quality assets while retaining the flexibility to return capital to stockholders.

We commenced operations in 2003 and have since devoted substantially all of our resources to research and development activities including developing our therapeutic platforms, identifying and developing potential product candidates and undertaking preclinical studies and clinical trials. Additionally, we have supported our research and development activities with general and administrative support, as well as by raising capital, conducting business planning and protecting our intellectual property. Other than the receipt of royalties on sales of zanidatamab and regulatory milestone payments relating to the regulatory approval of zanidatamab, we have not generated any revenue related to product approvals or the sale of approved products as of December 31, 2025, and, other than the anticipated receipt of additional royalties and potential regulatory milestone payments relating to future regulatory decisions and sales of zanidatamab, we do not expect to do so until such time as we or our strategic partners' obtain regulatory approval and commercialize one or more of our product candidates. We cannot be certain of the timing or success of approval of our product candidates.

Since our initial public offering ("IPO") in 2017, we have funded our operations primarily through follow-on public offerings, and private placements including the issuance of pre-funded warrants, and payments received under our license and collaboration agreements. Payments received or receivables from our license and collaboration agreements include upfront fees, milestone and royalty payments, as well as research support and reimbursement payments. Prior to our IPO, we also received financing from private equity placements and the issuance of convertible debt, which was subsequently converted into equity securities, and a credit facility. From inception to December 31, 2025, we received $1,026.3 million, net of equity issuance costs, from these sources of financing including proceeds from exercises of stock options and employee stock purchase plans. As of December 31, 2025, we had $270.6 million of cash resources consisting of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities.

Although it is difficult to predict our funding requirements, based upon our current operating plan, we anticipate that our existing cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities as of December 31, 2025, will enable us to fund our operating expenditures and capital expenditure requirements for at least the next twelve months from the date of this Annual Report on Form 10-K is filed with the SEC.

We reported a net loss of $81.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, and through December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $953.2 million. We expect to continue to incur operating losses in the near to medium term as we execute our strategic plan announced in 2025 (as discussed further in the section titled "Recent Developments" below), which emphasizes disciplined capital allocation, focused research and development investment, advancement of partnered programs, and active management of our royalty and asset portfolio. Our operating expense outlook reflects a multi-year planning framework designed to align spending with defined strategic priorities, including pipeline progression, technology platform advancement, and value-enhancing business development activities. We are prioritizing investments where we believe risk-adjusted returns are most attractive and expect operating expenses to be managed within this structured framework.

In January 2026, we announced our R&D priorities for 2026 and beyond, including our intention to continue conducting Phase 1 clinical studies for ZW191 and ZW251 in 2026. Advancement of other ADC programs, including potential clinical development of ZW220, ZW327, and ZW418, will be contingent on the availability of partnerships, collaborations, and/or external funding. We also announced that beyond 2026, we expect to focus our ADVANCE research efforts on multispecific antibody and engineered-cytokine platforms, funded partially with early-stage partnerships and collaborations. INDs for multispecific programs, ZW209 and ZW1528, remain on track for submission in 2026. We anticipate that development of wholly-owned preclinical candidates from our multispecific antibody portfolio should provide for one planned IND filing per annum commencing in 2028.

In November 2025, together with our partners Jazz and BeOne, we announced positive topline results from the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial supporting Ziihera as the potential HER2-targeted agent-of-choice and new standard of care in first-line HER2+ locally advanced or metastatic GEA regardless of PD-L1 status. The full results were subsequently presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology's Gastrointestinal Cancers Symposium in January 2026, where:

•Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy and Ziihera plus chemotherapy showed a clinically meaningful and statistically significant prolongation of progression-free survival (PFS) with approximately 35% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death versus trastuzumab and chemotherapy;
•Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful overall survival (OS) benefit with a median OS of more than two years (26.4 months); and

•At this first interim analysis, Ziihera plus chemotherapy showed a median OS of more than two years, with a strong trend toward statistical significance, favoring Ziihera plus chemotherapy versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. An additional planned OS interim analysis for Ziihera plus chemotherapy is currently expected in mid-2026.

Based on these data, our partner Jazz expects to complete the sBLA submission for zanidatamab in the first quarter of 2026 for the treatment of first-line HER2+ locally advanced or metastatic GEA under the real-time oncology review program in the United States where zanidatamab has been granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation for patients with HER2+ GEA. Jazz has also submitted these data for inclusion in the National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines (NCCN Guidelines). Upon regulatory review, Jazz expects a potential commercial launch for zanidatamab in 1L HER2+ GEA to take place in the second half of 2026.

In January 2026, Jazz updated enrollment guidance for EmpowHER-303 in which they expect to complete enrollment in the first half of 2027, with a top-line data readout later in 2027 or in early 2028. The EmpowHER-BC-303 study is a randomized clinical trial comparing zanidatamab plus physician's choice of chemotherapy against trastuzumab plus physician's choice of chemotherapy for the treatment of patients with metastatic HER+ breast cancer. Jazz is also pursuing collaborations with partners to combine zanidatamab with novel therapies. For example, the Phase 1 Beamion-BCGC1 trial (NCT06324357) in combination with Boehringer Ingelheim's zongertinib was recently initiated to explore the combination in metastatic HER2+ breast cancer, along with other potential tumor types.

In January 2026, the New Drug Submission ("NDS") for Ziihera was approved by Health Canada for the treatment of adults with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive (IHC 3+) biliary tract cancer, as monotherapy. Ziihera's market authorization has been issued with conditions, pending the results of trials to verify its clinical benefit. Subsequently, in February 2026 zanidatamab (Ziihera) was approved by the UK's Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) for the treatment of biliary tract cancer.

paragraphs: Zymeworks 是一家全球性生物技術公司，管理一組授權的醫療健康資產，並開發多樣化的新型多功能生物製劑，以改善難治疾病的照護標準，包括癌症、發炎及自身免疫疾病。我們相信我們的資產與版權集約策略，使我們與其他生物技術公司有所區別，因為這為我們提供了優化未來里程碑與版權現金流的機會，並選擇性投資高品質資產，同時保留回饋股東的靈活性。

我們的策略聚焦於透過 royalty 成長、戰略收購與內部創新來複利長期股東價值，並由嚴謹的資本配置與強化財務基礎所支撐，這財務基礎來自預期的里程碑付款與現有商業夥伴的版權收入。我們透過發現或收購並開發一組多樣化的臨牀前或臨牀階段醫療健康資產，同時評估戰略合作機會，將某些與臨牀開發及/或商業化相關的成本與風險轉移給戰略夥伴，並取得未來潛在版權與里程碑收入的權利。以下各項因素共同支撐我們策略的執行。
我們致力於運用在蛋白質工程與藥物化學方面的專業知識，發現並開發新一代的抗體基生物製劑，以解決重大未滿足的醫療需求，特別是在難治疾病領域。我們的專利結構導向分子建模技術，結合內部抗體發現與生成技術，支持一個完整的藥物開發引擎，能有效推進創新產品候選物的開發。
我們的多功能治療品項組合受到我們多特異性抗體治療品項（"MSATs"）與抗體藥物偶聯物（"ADCs"）技術平台的支持，這些技術平台使我們能開發新型治療品項，用於癌症、發炎及自身免疫疾病，並創造與新合作夥伴合作的機會。
合作夥伴與合作關係是我們策略的核心，作為持續研究與開發的資金來源，同時也減少對內部資本的依賴，以支持合作資產的後期臨牀開發。這些安排能分享風險，特別是在後期開發階段，並支持嚴謹的研發投資，這可以減少未來使用里程碑與版權付款來支應預計運作的必要性。
透過我們的資產與版權集約策略，我們致力於優化來自日益成長的授權產品與產品候選物組合的未來現金流，包括 Ziihera（zanidatamab-hrii）與 pasritamig。當合作治療品項進展至後期開發與商業化階段時，我們預期能成長出穩定且可預測的現金流，這些現金流可由我們運用，以追求對股東而言具有吸引力的風險調整後回報。
我們的資本配置策略聚焦於平衡對長期成長的投資與回饋股東的資本。當我們的版權組合成熟並產生超出運作與戰略投資需求的過剩資本時，我們保留靈活的機會將資本配置於股票回購。我們視股票回購為一種潛在工具，用以戰略性地減少我們的股票發行數量，並在長遠時間內提升總股東回報，同時持續優先投資能支持可持續價值創造的項目。關於資本回饋的決定，會在考量我們的流動性狀況、未來現金流展望及整體戰略目標的背景下進行評估。
我們有意評估並選擇性收購具有高品質資產或合作夥伴關係的計畫、技術、產品候選物及/或公司，這些與我們的戰略目標相符。透過運用我們的科學專業知識、開發能力與
透過營運效率，我們致力於提升資產價值並產生新的版稅收入。在評估收購機會時，我們考量多項因素，包括：
•戰略契合度；•版稅潛力；•差異化資產或平台；•解決未滿足醫療需求的潛力；
•足夠的智慧財產權保護；以及
我們維持一個合作計畫組合，利用我們的科技平台與科學專業知識，同時實現風險共擔與近端里程碑及版稅基準的回報潛力。

Zanidatamab，為本公司首個獲得監管核准的內部開發產品候選藥物，說明了我們以合作為基礎的執行方式。Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii)，為一種雙特異性抗體，針對表達 HER2 的腫瘤，使用我們的 Azymetric 平台開發，已顯示出正面的晚期臨牀結果，並在美國、中國、歐洲及加拿大等多個司法管轄區獲得治療 HER2 正向 ("HER2+") (IHC 3+) 膽道癌 ("BTC") 的監管核准。我們已與 BeOne Medicines Ltd. (原為 BeiGene, Ltd.，與其附屬公司合稱為 "BeOne") 及 Jazz Pharmaceuticals Ireland Limited，為 Jazz Pharmaceuticals plc 的子公司 (與其附屬公司合稱為 "Jazz") 籤訂單獨的合作與授權協議，授予各合作夥伴在不同地區獨家開發與商業化的權利。Jazz 計畫於 2026 年第一季完成 zanidatamab 的補充生物製品許可申請 ("sBLA") 提交，用於治療第一線 HER2+ 本地晚期或轉移性胃食道腺癌 ("GEA")，根據美國的實時癌症審查計畫，zanidatamab 已獲得治療 HER2+ GEA 患者的突破性療法指定。此外，zanidatamab 目前正在多個全球臨牀試驗中評估，用於治療更廣泛的 HER2 表達指徵，包括新輔助族羣、乳癌及其他 HER2 表達癌症。我們與 Jazz 和 BeOne 的合作關係，反映了我們透過合作推進內部發現計畫的策略，此策略可共擔開發風險，同時保留長期版稅及里程碑收入的潛力。

除了已收到的 53.0 百萬美元用於 Ziihera 在 BTC 的監管核准外，我們有權獲得來自 Jazz 和 BeOne 的近端里程碑付款，總計最高達 440.0 百萬美元，與 Ziihera 在美國、歐洲、日本及中國的 GEA 許可核准相關，如下：美國 - 250.0 百萬美元；歐洲 - 100.0 百萬美元；日本 - 75.0 百萬美元；中國 - 15.0 百萬美元。我們也預期，隨著在全球市場獲得 GEA 的監管核准，Ziihera 的銷售所產生的版稅收入將會增加。

paragraphs: 以下討論應配合附上的財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。本年度10-K申報書，包括以下各節，包含根據美國私人證券訴訟改革法案1995年及證券交易法所定義的向前看聲明。這些聲明受到風險與不確定性影響，可能導致實際結果與事件與這些向前看聲明所表達或暗示者有重大差異。有關這些風險與不確定性的詳細討論，請參閱本年度10-K申報書第1A項「風險因素」。我們提醒讀者不要過度依賴這些向前看聲明，這些聲明僅反映管理層於本年度10-K申報書日期的分析。我們不負有更新向前看聲明以反映發生於本年度10-K申報書日期之後的事件或情況的義務。關於我們財務狀況及營運成果於財務年度2024與財務年度2023的比較討論，已從本年度10-K申報書中省略，並引用自我們財務年度終了於2024年12月31日的年度10-K申報書，該申報書於2025年3月5日提交至美國證券交易委員會及加拿大各省與地區的證券委員會，並於「第二部分，第7項 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析」節中。
Zymeworks為一全球性生物技術公司，管理一組已授權的醫療保健資產，並開發多樣化的創新多功能生物製劑，以改善難以治療疾病的照護標準，包括癌症、發炎及自身免疫疾病。我們相信我們的資產與版權集約策略使我們與其他生物技術公司有所區別，因為這為我們提供機會優化未來里程碑與版權現金流，並選擇性投資於高品質資產，同時保留回饋股東的靈活性。

我們於2003年開始營運，並自那時起將幾乎所有資源投入研究與開發活動，包括開發我們的治療平台、識別與開發潛在產品候選品，以及進行非臨牀研究與臨牀試驗。此外，我們也透過一般及行政支援，以及透過籌資、進行業務規劃與保護我們的智慧財產權來支持研究與開發活動。除了從zanidatamab銷售所收取的版權以及zanidatamab的監管批准里程碑付款外，我們截至2025年12月31日尚未產生任何與產品批准或已批准產品銷售相關的收入。除了預期會收到更多zanidatamab銷售的版權及未來監管決定相關的潛在里程碑付款外，我們預期在取得我們或我們戰略夥伴的監管批准並商業化一個或多個產品候選品之前，不會產生此類收入。我們無法確定我們產品候選品的批准時間或成功性。

自我們於2017年進行首次公開發行（IPO）以來，我們主要透過後續公開發行、私人 placements（包括發行預資資金權證）以及根據我們的授權與合作協議所收到的付款來資助營運。根據我們的授權與合作協議所收到的付款或應收款項包括首付款、里程碑付款與版權付款，以及研究支援與補償付款。在進行IPO之前，我們也從私人股權 placements 及發行可轉換債務取得資金，這些債務後續轉換為 equity securities，以及取得信貸融資。從成立至2025年12月31日，我們從這些資金來源（包括股票選擇權行使及員工股票購買計劃的資金）收到淨額為1,026.3百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，我們擁有270.6百萬美元的現金資源，包括現金、現金等價物及市場可交易證券。
雖然很難預測我們的資金需求，根據我們目前的營運計畫，我們預期我們截至2025年12月31日的現金及現金等價物與市場可交易證券，將足以資助我們至少接下來十二個月的營運支出與資本支出需求。

我們於2025年12月31日財務年度報告淨損失為81.1百萬美元，且截至2025年12月31日，我們累積虧損為953.2百萬美元。我們預期在近至中短期內持續產生營運虧損，因為我們執行2025年宣佈的戰略計畫（如後述「近期發展」部分所討論），該計畫強調嚴謹的資本配置、聚焦的研究與開發投資、推進合作計畫，以及積極管理我們的版權與資產組合。我們的營運費用預測反映了一個多年度的規劃架構，用以將支出與明確的戰略優先事項對齊，包括管線進展、技術平台發展，以及價值提升的業務發展活動。我們優先投資於我們認為風險調整後回報最吸引人的領域，並預期營運費用將在這個結構化架構內進行管理。

2026年1月，我們宣佈了我們2026年及以後的研發優先事項，包括我們意圖於2026年繼續進行ZW191與ZW251的第1期臨牀研究。其他ADC計畫的進展，包括ZW220、ZW327與ZW418的潛在臨牀發展，將取決於合作夥伴、合作關係及/或外部資金的可用性。我們也宣佈，2026年後，我們預期將專注於ADVANCE研究計畫的多特異性單株抗體與工程化細胞激素平台，部分資金來自早期階段的合作夥伴與合作關係。多特異性計畫ZW209與ZW1528的IND（新藥申請）預計於2026年提交。我們預期，我們多特異性單株抗體組閤中完全擁有之非臨牀候選品的開發，應能提供每年一次的IND申請，自2028年起開始。
2025年11月，我們與合作夥伴Jazz及BeOne共同宣佈，來自Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01試驗的初步結果支持Ziihera作為HER2標靶治療的首選藥物及新的標準照護，在HER2+局部晚期或轉移性GEA的第一線治療中，不論PD-L1狀態如何。完整結果隨後於2026年1月的美國臨牀腫瘤學會（ASCO）消化道腫瘤學會大會上發表，其中：
•Ziihera 加上 tislelizumab 與化學治療，以及 Ziihera 加上化學治療，顯示出臨牀意義且統計上顯著延長進展-free survival (PFS)，與 trastuzumab 與化學治療相比，疾病進展或死亡風險降低約 35%；
•Ziihera 加上 tislelizumab 與化學治療顯示出統計上顯著且臨牀意義的總生存期 (OS) 好轉，中位數 OS 超過兩年 (26.4 個月)；
•在這次首次中期分析中，Ziihera 加上化學治療顯示出中位數 OS 超過兩年，顯示出強烈的統計顯著趨勢，Ziihera 加上化學治療優於 trastuzumab 加上化學治療。Ziihera 加上化學治療的另一個預計 OS 中期分析目前預期在 2026 年中進行。

根據這些數據，我們的合作夥伴 Jazz 預期在 2026 年第一季完成 zanidatamab 的 sBLA 提交，用於治療第一線 HER2+ 本地晚期或轉移性 GEA，並在美國的 real-time oncology review 程序中進行審查，zanidatamab 已獲 Breakthrough Therapy Designation 用於 HER2+ GEA 患者。Jazz 也已提交這些數據以納入 National Comprehensive Cancer Network 指南 (NCCN Guidelines)。在監管審查後，Jazz 預期 zanidatamab 在 1L HER2+ GEA 的潛在商業上市可能在 2026 年下半年進行。

在 2026 年 1 月，Jazz 更新了 EmpowHER-303 的入組指引，預期在 2027 年上半年完成入組，並在 2027 年後期或 2028 年初進行初步數據分析。EmpowHER-BC-303 研究是一項隨機臨牀試驗，比較 zanidatamab 加上醫師選擇的化學治療與 trastuzumab 加上醫師選擇的化學治療，用於治療患有轉移性 HER+ 乳癌的患者。Jazz 也在尋求與合作夥伴合作，將 zanidatamab 與新興治療方式結合。例如，Phase 1 Beamion-BCGC1 試驗 (NCT06324357) 與 Boehringer Ingelheim 的 zongertinib 結合，最近已啟動，用於探索在轉移性 HER2+ 乳癌中的組合，以及其它潛在的腫瘤類型。

在 2026 年 1 月，Ziihera 的新藥申請 ("NDS") 已經獲加拿大衛生部批准，用於治療曾接受治療、無法手術切除的局部晚期或轉移性 HER2 陽性 (IHC 3+) 膽道癌成人患者，作為單一療法。Ziihera 的市場許可已發出，但需待試驗結果驗證其臨牀效益。隨後，在 2026 年 2 月，zanidatamab (Ziihera) 已經獲英國藥物及醫療器材規範管理局 (MHRA) 批准，用於治療膽道癌。
